newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 1.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* A federal judge has blocked efforts by Staples to acquire Office Depot, citing antitrust grounds.
* The Dow Jones Industrials gained 18.99 percent in the first half.
* General Motors, Ford Motor Co and Chrysler are expected to post weak sales for the month of June.
* JP Foodservice has agreed to acquire Rykoff-Sexton for $1.4 billion in stock and assumed debt.
* The Financial Accounting Standards Board may hold off on its threat to restrict or abolish "poolings of interest," which is used to account for big stock mergers.
* Ford Motor Co and Citicorp plans to discontinue their joint venture offering credit-card users rebates toward buying a new car.
* Compaq introduced two personal computers priced below $1,000, a sign that low-priced machines are on the move.
* Andersen Worldwide, seeing two of its CEO nominees rebuffed by partners, has named Robert Grafton as the interim CEO and have put the electoral process on hold.
* A World Trade Organization appeals board on Monday decided against Canada in a dispute with the United States involving a regional edition of Time Warner Inc's Sports Illustrated.
* Campbell Soup named Dale Morrison president and chief executive.
* An alleged racketeer involved in Nomura scandal has fingered three other large firms, threatening to broaden the controversy in Japan's securities industry.
* Eli Lilly and Co plans to begin running advertisements to boost sales of its anti-depressant drug, Prozac.
* Seagram Co Ltd and Viacom have submitted competing plans for the breakup of their USA Networks cable-television partnership.
* Heard on the Street: Polo Ralph Lauren started off hot when it debuted with its initial public offering. But since then, it's been downhill, marking a rapid up-and-down for the firm.
* Credit Markets: Bond prices fell amid fears that economy is gearing up again and that possibly at least one interest-rate increase is likely to occur before the end of the year.
